text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- King Hussein emphasises during a tour of the kingdom's border area with Iraq the need to solve the problem of cross-border smuggling "firmly" and says that Jordan will not be lenient with smugglers.
- Friday is the start of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan, king gets flood of congratulatory cables.
- King congratulates Syrian President on his recovery from surgery.
- Prime Minister Kabariti tells senators in the upper chamber during the debate on the 1997 budget that Jordan has succeeded in attaining a just society.
- Supply Minister decides to fix flour prices to bakeries and lowers prices of retail sugar in line with softer global prices.
- Jordan's Islamist-dominated union of professional association calls on people to perform Friday prayers close to the area near the Israeli trade fair in protest against it.
- Chief religious judge Tamimmi calls on Jordanians to be more compassionate and caring towards others during Ramadan.
- Crown Prince Hassan to deliver a speech in the Mediterranean charter conference to be held in Madrid which will urge greater cooperation between the states of the area.
